answer: Rate-scaled puzzle registration accepts an agent only with a valid solution to a per-epoch cipher seeded by recent registrations and a unique salt. Difficulty follows D(n)=base×2^(n/100), so early identities are cheap and later ones costly; an attacker cannot harbor many without paying rising GPU-seconds and delay. Each identity also needs a unique quartz-oscillator timing nonce, so cloned solutions fail and the attacker pays per machine, not once.
